A.explanation: At $t = 6 \text{ s}$ the goods train has travelled $60 \text{ m}$ but the express has travelled only $0.25 \times 6^2 = 9 \text{ m}$, so it is still far behind.

B.explanation: At $t = 10 \text{ s}$ the goods train has travelled $100 \text{ m}$ but the express has travelled only $0.25 \times 10^2 = 25 \text{ m}$.

C.explanation: At $t = 20 \text{ s}$ the express reaches $v = at = 10 \text{ m s}^{-1}$, so it only just equals the goods train speed and has travelled only $100 \text{ m}$ against $200 \text{ m}$ for the goods train.

D.explanation: At $t = 40 \text{ s}$ both have travelled $400 \text{ m}$, with $10t = 0.25t^2$, so the displacements are equal and overtaking occurs.

hints: Notice what overtake means here: both trains start at the same station at $t = 0$, so their displacements $s$ from the station must be equal at time $t$.
Write $s$ for each train: goods train at constant $10 \text{ m s}^{-1}$ gives $s = vt$, while express starting from rest with $a = 0.5 \text{ m s}^{-2}$ gives $s = \frac{1}{2}at^2$.
Set $10t = \frac{1}{2} \times 0.5 \times t^2$ and solve for the non-zero $t$ by cancelling one factor of $t$.
walkthrough: Goods train has constant velocity, so displacement from the station is $s_g = vt = 10t$, with $s$ in $\text{m}$ and $t$ in $\text{s}$.
Express train starts from rest with uniform acceleration, so use $s = ut + \frac{1}{2}at^2$ with $u = 0$ and $a = 0.5 \text{ m s}^{-2}$ to get $s_e = 0 + \frac{1}{2} \times 0.5 \times t^2 = 0.25t^2$.
Overtake means same position at same time, so set $s_e = s_g$: $0.25t^2 = 10t$.
Check: $s_g = 10 \times 40 = 400 \text{ m}$ and $s_e = 0.25 \times 40^2 = 400 \text{ m}$, confirming equal displacement. This is option D.
